title: The Talkative Tortoise
text:
A tortoise lived in a lake with two geese who were her close friends. Then came a drought. The lake shrank day by day, and the geese decided to fly to another lake that still had plenty of water. The tortoise begged them not to leave her behind to die in the mud.

The geese came up with a plan. They found a stout stick. The tortoise would grip the middle of it firmly in her mouth, and the two geese would each take one end in their beaks and carry her through the air. There was only one condition: whatever happened, she must not open her mouth. She promised.

So they rose into the sky and flew over the countryside. As they passed above a town, people below looked up, pointed and laughed. Look, they shouted, the geese are carrying a tortoise on a stick! What a strange sight!

The tortoise was annoyed. She wanted to tell them it was none of their business. She opened her mouth to answer, let go of the stick, fell to the ground, and was killed. In the Jataka version, the story is told to a king who could not stop talking, and he took the hint.
lesson: A good plan can be ruined by one moment of indiscipline. When you have committed to staying quiet or patient, do not let someone's mockery provoke you into letting go.
